title: Dashboard: three structures
question: Each one answers "what have I spent this month, or last full month?" first. They all use the same shared components, so all ten themes carry each of them. Lock one, steer, or re-roll.

options.label: Two-month statement
options.thesis: This month so far, set against the last full month, category by category on one shared spine.
options.viewport: A sentence headline (spent so far, against the same day last month), then back-to-back category bars: this month grows left, last month grows right, the change between them. A right rail holds income, net cash flow, savings, net worth and anything that needs fixing.

raised.raise: One chart grammar for the whole page: every bar shares one baseline, one scale and one gap, so the eye compares lengths, never styles.

options.risk: Early in the month the left side is short, so it needs a 'by this day last month' tick to stay fair.

options.label: Month pivot
options.lineage: the spreadsheet pivot you would build by hand
options.thesis: Six months of spending in one table. This month is the live column, and each category is measured against its own usual.
options.viewport: The month's total and pace up top. Below, a categories-by-months table: cells shade by how far they sit from that row's median, the current month is outlined as '18 of 31 days', and any cell drills into its transactions.
options.risk: A table first can read as a spreadsheet. Without a clear headline, it buries the one number you came for.

options.label: Spending calendar
options.lineage: a wall calendar with the month's receipts pinned to it
options.thesis: The month as a calendar: what you spent each day, with the rest of the month's known payments already pencilled in.
options.viewport: Month total and pace headline. A 7-by-5 day grid, each cell showing that day's spend with a fill bar. Future days show expected recurring payments in dashed outline. A right rail ranks the month's categories and lists the selected day's transactions.
options.risk: Days lead and categories follow, so 'where did it go' depends on the right rail.
